pages.text: The little lamb at Pipo's farm wore a tiny bell. It jingled with every step.
But today the lamb was not in the pen. "I will find you for sure." Pipo set off toward the hill.
Mrs. Goose stretched her long neck. "I saw it by the stream earlier! Definitely."
Only running water sounded by the stream. She tilted her head. "Oh? It was surely here."
"Then under the big tree! I saw it there too." She waddled ahead.
Only two crows were beneath the tree. Mrs. Goose flapped her wings. "Oh, not here either?"
Her story grew longer. "So, in the morning... no, perhaps at lunchtime..."
Pipo pricked his ears. Somewhere, jingle, jingle.
He looked behind the bush where the sound came from. The lamb was grazing, its bell jingling.
Pipo brought the lamb home. Mrs. Goose was already far away, spreading the news. "Pipo found it, you know!"
